newsitem.title: UK: IPE April Brent expires at $20.14, up 25 cts.
newsitem.headline: IPE April Brent expires at $20.14, up 25 cts.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures settled up 25 cents on Friday on book-squaring ahead of the April contract expiry and news of slimmer April North Sea loading programmes, traders said.
The front-month April contract expired at $20.14 a barrel. May settled at $19.74, 11 cents off the high.

The April/May spread ended at 40 cents, down from 49 cents in the morning but well above just a few cents at one point earlier in the week. May/June ended at 14 cents compared with seven or eight on Thursday.

Brent futures had resumed trading at $20.11 a barrel an hour before the close at 1915 GMT after business was halted for 55 minutes due to a power cut. April had stopped at $20.12 when the outage occurred at 1813 GMT.
After the resumption April Brent rose to trade at $20.30 a barrel at 1920 GMT as prices caught up with gains that had been made on NYMEX crude during the suspension of trading.
IPE gas oil closed up 25 cents, posting a lame performance that only just tracked stronger Brent and U.S. heating oil.
Front month April gas oil settled at $169.50 a tonne, 50 cents shy of the high and 75 cents off the low.

Markets rose on Thursday after news April's Brent loading programme would be eight cargoes lighter than March. Traders said strength on Friday was partly a follow-through from that. -- William Maclean London newsroom +44 171 542 7646
